incidents.cause: The passenger’s failure to avoid the rotating propeller after exiting the airplane.  Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s failure to include deplaning procedures as part of the passenger safety briefing.
The student pilot's improper recovery from a bounced landing.
The pilot’s improper flare, which resulted in a hard landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s improper decision to land during a thunderstorm.
The pilot did not maintain directional control during a water touchdown.

A total loss of engine power during cruise flight resulting from the failure of a fuel line. Contributing to the accident was inadequate maintenance inspections that failed to detect the deteriorating fuel line.

A total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have resulted in the loss of engine power.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during takeoff.
The failure of the pilots onboard the airplane to see and avoid the helicopter while maneuvering in the traffic pattern, which resulted in a midair collision.
The flight instructor’s unstabilized approach during an autorotation that resulted in hard landing.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain control during the landing approach.
The pilot’s failure to maintain helicopter control while on the ground when his attention was diverted, which resulted in a dynamic rollover.
